solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Second stroke in poor handwriting

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher marks down a second careless pen-stroke in a pupil's messy writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests a pen movement, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is untidy, hurried writing that is hard to read.

clue.text: Cover unconventional novel in English exercise

indicators.note: in says the scrambled word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: an unconventional arrangement of the word novel puts its letters out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A student wraps an offbeat novel inside an English workbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unconventional' scrambles the novel; 'in' slips those letters between the two abbreviations. 'exercise' suggests homework, but it is school PE.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is a paper wrapper or covering, especially for a letter.

clue.text: Anticipate new trouble with wife about love

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first pieces surround the letter for love

parts.note: fresh means new
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone foresees fresh marital trouble over a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sets the love letter just after the first letter of the opening piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow is to hint at or prefigure an event before it happens, so it serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Flower in ruins periodically visited

indicators.note: visiting the letters periodically means taking every other one, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A tourist calls now and then at a flower growing among ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: Tot playing with rare cat that's reddish brown

indicators.note: playing about with the letters lets them be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A toddler plays with an unusual cat that has a ginger-brown coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is fired clay, and by extension its brownish-orange colour.

clue.text: Son with child in uncontrolled move

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A father and young child lose control together, perhaps on ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a vehicle's sliding motion that the driver cannot control.

clue.text: New driver engaged in obsessive behaviour in Asian capital

indicators.note: engaged in means held inside, so the driver's letter goes into the other word

parts.note: a mania is an obsessive enthusiasm
L is the learner plate, marking a new driver in Britain

explanation.surface: A learner driver is gripped by road rage on the streets of an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate, so L stands for a new driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is the capital city of the Philippines.

clue.text: Source of advice on dog without lead in crowd

parts.note: CAB is the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British charity offering free advice

indicators.note: without its lead means the first letter, the one at the head, is dropped

parts.note: a poodle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Someone seeks advice about a dog that has slipped its lead in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash but means the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Caboodle means a group or lot, as in 'the whole caboodle', loosely a crowd.

clue.text: Hundred following correct route in large hall

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
on course describes following the correct route

explanation.surface: A hundred people trace the right path through a vast hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is not a placement word here: it belongs to the phrase meaning 'on course'.
explanation.definitionFit: A concourse is a big open area in a station or building where people gather.

clue.text: Lover of eucalyptus stunning a large area

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is a stunning blow

explanation.surface: A tree lover is wowed by a vast stretch of gum forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunning' looks like praise but means knocking out, KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Koalas feed almost entirely on gum-tree leaves, so they are devoted fans of that plant.

clue.text: Evergreen set with energy boarding a ship

indicators.note: boarding means getting on to, so these pieces go into the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is the steamship prefix
to gel is to set firm
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A shrub is set on a ship's deck with plenty of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen used figuratively means never seeming to grow old, i.e. timeless.

clue.text: Perch good in carnival location for composer

parts.note: a perch or rod is an old unit of length

indicators.note: in places the letter for good inside the city's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosts a famous carnival

explanation.surface: A fish is landed at a carnival city by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a fish or a resting place, but here it is the old length unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Joaquín Rodrigo was the Spanish composer of the Concierto de Aranjuez.

clue.text: Money falling short in card game

indicators.note: falling short means cut off before the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: loot is slang for money

explanation.surface: A gambler runs out of cash during a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Loo is an old gambling card game, related to whist, played for stakes.

clue.text: Top brass in tight order

parts.note: tight and high are both informal words for drunk
a command is an order

explanation.surface: Senior officers run a very tight ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' suggests strict, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The high command is the senior leadership of an army, i.e. the generals or top officers.

clue.text: Grand study of stars and good eating

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
astronomy is the science of the stars

explanation.surface: A splendid evening of stargazing followed by a fine dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the art and practice of choosing and enjoying fine food.

clue.text: Agree under £500 for smart wear

indicators.note: under, in a down clue, puts this piece below the sum of money

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
to suit is to agree with or fit

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a budget of under five hundred pounds for a sharp outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under £500' reads as a price limit, but places SUIT beneath MONKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkey suit is jokey slang for formal evening dress or a dinner jacket.

clue.text: Dash from top player grabbing first of prizes

indicators.note: grabbing means taking hold of, so the letter goes inside the player's word

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked tennis player

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A star player rushes off clutching a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed means haste, and to dash is to move with great haste, as nouns too.

clue.text: Particular spice with cooking starts to flavour Indian curry

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement
starts to signals taking the initial letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for one exact spice to flavour an Indian curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific and particular both mean exact or relating to one definite thing.

clue.text: Arrange group in rosettes

definitions.meaning: to set is to put in place or arrange
a set is a group of things that belong together

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the next word

explanation.surface: A florist organises a batch of rosettes for the show.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Arrange' and 'group' define the answer; the hidden word supports them.
explanation.definitionFit: Set works as a verb meaning arrange, and as a noun meaning a collection or group.

clue.text: Spanish gent cycling from opposite part of Europe?

indicators.note: cycling means letters are carried round from the front to the back of the word

parts.note: señor is Spanish for gentleman

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman cycles all the way to the far end of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves SE from the front of SENOR to the end. Scandinavia lies at the opposite end of Europe from Spain, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse describes Scandinavia, in Europe's far north, as opposed to Spain in the south-west.

clue.text: Judge tidiness in sports ground?

parts.note: the rec is the British short form of recreation ground
order means neatness or tidiness

explanation.surface: A referee rules on how neat the playing field looks.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a Recorder is a part-time Crown Court judge. The 'in' is loose: the tidiness is in the ground figuratively, not placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Recorder is a barrister or solicitor sitting as a part-time criminal judge in England.

clue.text: We bear logs awkwardly close to house? Hard work

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters are clumsily jumbled into a new order
close to here means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Two people struggle to carry firewood up to the house: hard graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges WE BEAR LOGS into ELBOWGREAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow grease is an idiom for strenuous physical effort, especially cleaning or polishing.

clue.text: Stir with book on fraud in the East End

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the book's letter above the rest
London's East End Cockney accent drops the opening h of words

parts.note: a hustle is a swindle or fraud

explanation.surface: Someone causes a stir by publishing a book about a scam in East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their h's.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustle means busy activity or commotion, and a stir is a fuss or commotion.

clue.text: International restriction

definitions.meaning: a player chosen for a national team is awarded a ...
an upper limit, as on spending

explanation.surface: A cross-border limit, like a trade quota.
explanation.definitionFit: Cap means a selection for a national side, and also a limit placed on something.

clue.text: Refinement in language

explanation.surface: Elegance in one's choice of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish is both refined manners and the national language spoken in Poland.

clue.text: Nuns I list (not half) in order showing secretion

indicators.note: putting them in order means rearranging the letters
not half means only half the word is kept, the first two letters

explanation.surface: A nun puts her sisters on a rota, but only half the list is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' leaves LI from LIST; 'in order' shuffles NUNS I LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is a hormone secreted by the pancreas to regulate blood sugar.

clue.text: Flaw noticed somewhat in garden feature

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gardener spots a blemish in part of the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is the area of mown grass found in most gardens.

clue.text: Flier, leading light after one's gone in part of ship

indicators.note: in places the shortened star inside the ship part

parts.note: the keel runs along the bottom of a ship

indicators.note: after one is gone means the letter A, one, is removed

parts.note: a star is a leading light

explanation.surface: A pilot, once the captain has left, takes the lead on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the letter A here, and 'in' splits the ship part around the shortened leading light.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small hovering falcon, a bird and so a flier.

clue.text: Former wicketkeeper, we hear, in difficulty

indicators.note: we hear tells us it is the spoken sound of the name that counts

parts.note: Alan Knott kept wicket for England in cricket in the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: A retired wicketkeeper is said to be in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A wicketkeeper is the cricket fielder who stands behind the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a tangle, and by extension a problem or difficulty.

clue.text: Relative expertise of a barrister?

definitions.meaning: a barrister's skill lies ..., read as two words

explanation.surface: A family member who happens to be a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-law is a relation by marriage, such as a spouse's parent.

clue.text: Some don is volatile showing temperamental nature

indicators.note: volatile means unstable, so the letters are unsettled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A certain academic's hot temper shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Moodiness is a tendency to swing between sulky or irritable states.
